data.one_liner: Run FFmpeg and FFprobe commands from Dart with prebuilt audio codecs for multiple platforms.
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter applications to execute FFmpeg and FFprobe commands to process media. This variant is focused specifically on audio codecs such as mp3, opus, vorbis, and speex. Prebuilt binaries are provided for Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
use_when: You need to process audio files or streams using FFmpeg inside a Flutter application
You want prebuilt native libraries for audio codecs without compiling FFmpeg yourself
avoid_when: You need video codecs (use the video or full variants instead)
You need GPL-licensed codecs like x264 or x265 (use a -gpl variant instead)
strengths: Provides a single unified Dart API across Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, and Linux
Prebuilt native libraries mean no compilation needed during build time
Includes logs, statistics, and completion callbacks for sessions
weaknesses: Large binary size due to bundled native FFmpeg libraries
Platform-specific setup requirements like minimum OS versions or package prerequisites on Linux
data.setup_notes: Requires minimum platform versions (Android API 24, iOS 14.0, macOS 10.15, Windows 10). Linux requires installing additional development packages like libjson-glib-dev.

alternatives.name: just_audio
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need to play audio rather than perform advanced FFmpeg transcoding and processing operations.

alternatives.name: audioplayers
alternatives.why_pick_it: For simple audio playback use cases where a full FFmpeg wrapper is overkill.

alternatives.name: video_player
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need standard platform-backed video/audio playback instead of media manipulation.
